lines: A four-pole ladder filter whose response is set by a five-channel signal at the FILTER TOPOLOGY jack: a dry level and a level for each pole, mixed to make any filter shape
Sets the cutoff over ten octaves with C4 at 261.63Hz in the middle, one octave to a turn of the dial, held between 1Hz and 18% of the sample rate
Sets the resonance, 0 to 1 on the dial; the figure is squared and multiplied by ten inside, so self-oscillation comes only near the top
Scales the voltage at the cutoff CV jack, -1 to +1, before it is added to the cutoff in octaves
Scales the voltage at the resonance CV jack, -1 to +1, before a tenth of it is added to the resonance
Shifts the cutoff at one octave per volt, scaled by the trimpot above it
Shifts the resonance, 10V covering the whole of the dial's travel through the trimpot above it; the total is held between 0 and 1
The signal to be filtered, with ±5V taken as full scale
A five-channel signal setting the filter response: the first channel is the dry level and the next four are the level of each pole; with nothing patched the filter is a four-pole lowpass
The filtered signal at ±5V, soft-clipped on the way out
Note — with nothing patched to FILTER TOPOLOGY this is a plain four-pole lowpass; a Personality module on that jack is what makes it anything else
Note — the topology signal is read every sample, so crossfaders, switches and slew limiters can morph the filter shape on the way in
Note — 0.3125V on a topology channel is unity for that pole, since the mix is divided by ten thirty-seconds before it is clipped
Note — the number of channels at the audio input sets the channel count of the output
Menu — Add Morphscope (right side) — places a Morphscope expander immediately to the right of this module

0.why: PoleDancer.cpp:214 reads it with getPolyVoltageSimd, multiplies by the trimpot and adds it to the cutoff in octaves at line 216

1.why: PoleDancer.cpp:209 reads it with getPolyVoltageSimd, divides by 10, multiplies by the trimpot, adds the knob and clamps the total to 0..1

2.why: PoleDancer.cpp:204 reads it with getVoltageSimd and divides by 5; line 202 takes the channel count from it

3.why: PoleDancer.cpp:139-156 reads up to five channels as the mix weights, and sets a four-pole lowpass when the jack is unpatched

0.why: PoleDancer.cpp:225 writes five times the clipped mix and line 229 sets the channel count from the audio input

PoleDancer.notes: The filter core is Fundamental's VCF, with the four state variables mixed by the five weights instead of a fixed tap (PoleDancer.cpp:72-82). The mix is divided by POLEMIX_VOLTAGE_SCALE, 10/32, so a channel at 0.3125V is unity for that pole and anything higher drives the clipper. The cutoff dial reads out as hertz and counts one octave to a turn.

lines: Holds one filter shape and sends it to a Pole Dancer as a five-channel signal: a dry level and a level for each of the four poles
The five levels on one five-channel cable, written at a divided rate rather than every sample
Note — this module holds no filter until one is loaded: right-click it and choose a preset, which is also what fills in the name on the display
Note — the five levels have no controls on this panel; they come from the presets, or from an Architect expander placed immediately to the right
Note — the name on the display can be typed into, and it is saved with the preset
Note — because the five levels travel as one polyphonic cable, ordinary crossfaders, switches and slew limiters can morph between filter shapes on the way to the Pole Dancer
Menu — Add Architect (right side) — places an Architect expander immediately to the right of this module

0.why: PoleDancerPersonality.cpp:96-97 sets the channel count to five and writes the five level values

PoleDancerPersonality.notes: None of the five level parameters has a widget on this panel, so none of them can be clicked for help; they are reached through the presets or through the Architect expander. The output is written only on the expander clock divider tick rather than every sample (PoleDancerPersonality.cpp:61 and 94).

lines: An expander for Pole Dancer that draws the filter response that module is working with; it goes immediately to the right of it
Sets how much of the plot is shown: narrow, mid or wide
Chooses what the screen draws: Bode, the magnitude and phase against frequency, or Pole/Zero, the roots on the s-plane
Note — with no Pole Dancer immediately to its left this module reads nothing and the screen shows an empty plot
Note — the mix and feedback figures it plots are sent over from the Pole Dancer; they have no controls on this panel and nothing here changes them
Note — the plot is refreshed on a divided clock rather than every sample, so fast movement in the topology signal is smoothed over
PoleDancerWorkbench-PoleDancer.notes: Nine of this module's eleven parameters have no widget on the panel: the five mix levels and four feedback figures are written into it by the Pole Dancer to its left (PoleDancerWorkbench.cpp:166-175), so only the two switches can be clicked. The same class also builds the Architect, which does give the mix levels trimpots.

lines: An expander for Personality that draws a filter response and gives it five trimpots to build one with; it goes immediately to the right of the Personality
Sets the dry level of the filter being built, 0 to 32 as the panel marks it, and hands it back to the Personality
Sets the level of pole one, 0 to 32 as the panel marks it, and hands it back to the Personality
Sets the level of pole two, 0 to 32 as the panel marks it, and hands it back to the Personality
Sets the level of pole three, 0 to 32 as the panel marks it, and hands it back to the Personality
Sets the level of pole four, 0 to 32 as the panel marks it, and hands it back to the Personality
Sets how much of the plot is shown: narrow, mid or wide
Chooses what the screen draws: Bode, the magnitude and phase against frequency, or Pole/Zero, the roots on the s-plane
Note — with no Personality immediately to its left this module draws nothing and its trimpots reach nothing
Note — the Personality takes charge for one cycle whenever it is connected or a patch is loaded, so its own values land on these trimpots then; after that the trimpots drive the Personality
Note — 32 on a trimpot is a gain of 32 on that pole, so small settings go a long way and full ones can be very loud
Note — to build a filter, set the five trimpots here, type a name on the Personality, and save that as a preset
Note — the four pole feedback figures the plot uses have no control on this panel and are not sent over by the Personality, so they stay at zero here
PoleDancerWorkbench-Personality.notes: The trimpots are configured as a 0 to 10 parameter shown as a percentage, while the panel marks them 0 to 32: PoleDancerWorkbench.cpp:40-42 multiplies the value by 32/10 to get the coefficient, which is the figure the panel gives. The four feedback parameters have no widget and the Personality never writes them (PoleDancerPersonality.cpp:70-76 sends only the five values), so the pole-zero plot here is drawn with no feedback.
